comment: What a correctly installed Layer 1 looks like from the outside, so the installer and the doctor
cannot disagree. This file is ours: it describes Serena, it contains none of it.
Each fix names a file under Serena's site-packages and a sentinel - a distinctive string the fix
introduces. A sentinel survives rewording of the code around it, which reverse-applying a diff does
not; that was an earlier version of this check and it failed on a machine patched by hand before the
script existed. Paths are relative to site-packages unless 'root' says otherwise: 'home' means the
SENTINELS ARE VERSION-SHAPED, and this file was re-derived against the 2.x fork. Two of the six
changed FILE between 1.7.0 and 2.x, and one changed its log wording - with the 1.7.0 sentinels the
doctor reported a working C# fix as absent. If you move to another Serena, re-derive these by
grepping the installed package rather than trusting this file.
WE SHIP NO SERENA CODE. The fixes arrive as commits on the fork named in 'source', installed with
uv. Serena is GPL-3.0-or-later from v2 (solidlsp stays MIT), so shipping patches against it would
make this MIT repository carry GPL-derived files - see NOTICE.md.

source.why: Every fix below is a commit on that branch, intended to go upstream; one already has (is_ignored_path, upstream f0693a10). On 1.7.0 these were hand patches that every 'uv tool upgrade' silently reverted.
source.licence: Upstream is per component: solidlsp MIT, the Serena application GPL-3.0-or-later from v2. The fork inherits that unchanged. v1.7.0 (tag mit-final) is the last MIT release.

versionNote: Read EVERY dist-info, and prefer direct_url.json for which build it actually is. Two reasons. An in-place upgrade can leave the old dist-info beside the new one. And a packaged app's shell sees a UNION of its own redirected copy and the real one: on the machine this was written on, the real site-packages holds serena_agent-2.0.0.dev0 alone and the app container's private copy holds serena_agent-1.7.0 alone, but a shell inside the container lists BOTH at the same absolute path - so taking the first match reports 1.7.0, a build that is not serving anything. That is the trap the installer's redirection probe refuses over, and the same one as 'uv tool list' naming a stale copy.

fixes.matters: Without it Serena walks the whole engine tree on every freshness check, about 190s per symbolic call on ours.

fixes.sentinel: .csproj file(s) matched by the project's ignore settings
fixes.matters: Without it the C# server opens every .csproj in the engine, ThirdParty included.
fixes.note: The 1.7.0 sentinel was the old log wording, 'skipped %d .csproj under ignored_paths'. It matches nothing on 2.x, where the fix is present and reworded - so the old sentinel reported a working fix as absent.

fixes.matters: Without it an unscoped find_symbol walks the tree for hours after the client has given up, and has crashed clangd.
fixes.note: Lived in serena/tools/symbol_tools.py on 1.7.0. Upstream closed the issue as not planned, so this one stays local.

fixes.matters: The fast whole-tree symbol lookup, about 0.1s from clangd's index. Absent, every definition question falls back to a file walk.
fixes.note: The 2.x port carries three fixes the 1.7.0 patch never had: it never returns a bare empty list, one failing language server cannot sink the whole call, and the default language is cpp.

fixes.matters: Without it one transient accept() error kills the HTTP listener while the process keeps running, so the server looks healthy and answers nothing.
fixes.note: Was a sitecustomize.py shim on 1.7.0. Now a module called from serena/cli.py before the event loop serves, which is why it survives a reinstall.

fixes.matters: The stock claude-code context excludes search_for_pattern, which is the only route to TODOs and inline notes. A routing table naming it then points at a tool that does not exist.
fixes.note: NOT a patch and not in the fork. The installer derives it on your machine from your installed stock context, so this repository ships no copy of it. Any context carrying search_for_pattern will do - a team may run one under its own name - and the server must be started with --context <that name>.

fixes.matters: Startup joins every language server under one shared deadline instead of waiting unbounded, and a server that fails or times out is recorded and skipped while the rest keep running. Without it one slow server holds up all of them, and a query naming a language whose server never started is answered by a DIFFERENT server - a wrong answer rather than an error. Commit cbac10b2 on the fork. The sentinel is a log literal rather than an exception message on purpose: prose gets reworded, and this file already carries one fix whose log line changed between versions so the old sentinel reported a WORKING fix as absent. The fork registers this literal as frozen and will say so at its registration if it ever has to move.
